title: An arena
description:
General-purpose `new` has to find a suitable free block every time, and track it so it can be freed later. When many small things are allocated together and thrown away together (everything needed to draw one frame, or to answer one request), there is a far faster scheme: take one big block and hand out pieces by moving a pointer along it. Freeing is a single reset of that pointer.

Write `class Arena`:

- `explicit Arena(std::size_t capacity)`: owns one buffer of that many bytes (a `std::unique_ptr<std::byte[]>` is fine).
- `void* allocate(std::size_t bytes, std::size_t alignment)`: returns the next free address that is a multiple of `alignment`, and moves past it. Returns `nullptr` if there is not enough room. `alignment` is a power of two.
- `template <typename T, typename... Args> T* create(Args&&... args)`: allocates room for a `T` with the right alignment and constructs it there; returns `nullptr` if it does not fit.
- `std::size_t used() const`, `std::size_t capacity() const`.
- `void reset()`: everything is free again. (Objects are **not** destroyed, so an arena suits types with nothing to clean up.)

To round a position up to a multiple of a power-of-two alignment: `(position + alignment - 1) & ~(alignment - 1)`. Align the real **address**, not just the offset.
lessonTitle: Custom Memory: Placement new, Allocators and PMR
